extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO practitioners, law firms, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, findings, and sanctions used in a USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline final order addressing a practitioner's mishandling of funds, noncompliance with firm policies, and alleged professional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation of statutory and regulatory authority establishing the Office's power to adjudicate and impose discipline in practitioner matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent attorney is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration (e.g., Reg. No. 53,814) brings a practitioner under the USPTO's professional conduct rules and disciplinary jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) includes engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct; in this case identified as (i) receiving funds on behalf of the law firm and not immediately informing the law firm about the funds or remitting the funds but, instead, depositing them into a personal account with the intent of remitting the funds to the law firm at a later time and (ii) not complying with the law firm's policy regarding the use of its deposit account or promptly informing the law firm of his use of its deposit account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly finds that the specified handling of funds and failure to follow firm deposit-account policies constitute violations of §10.23(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to promptly inform the law firm and remit funds received on the firm's behalf
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner should promptly inform the law firm of monies received on the law firm's behalf and promptly remit the entire amount of monies received to the law firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by facts where Respondent received $6,250 from two clients, deposited checks into personal account(s), did not inform or timely remit to the firm, and only delivered funds after the firm questioned him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose new client matters and open separate client files
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm policy required disclosure of new client matters and opening of separate client files; a practitioner must comply with that policy and disclose when preparing/filing new work (e.g., a continuation-in-part application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose and open a file resulted in the law firm not knowing about the CIP application and is cited as misconduct in the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify client file number when using firm's deposit account
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the law firm's deposit account, the practitioner was required to identify the client file number as part of authorized use of the account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent used the firm's deposit account to pay USPTO fees ($462) but did not timely inform the firm or identify the client file number, breaching the firm's policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of a firm's deposit account conditioned on compliance with firm policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a firm deposit account is permitted only for authorized purposes and provided that the practitioner complies with the firm's policy regarding such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The firm's permission was conditional; noncompliance (e.g., failure to identify file number or inform firm) constitutes a breach of duty and basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and ordered (public reprimand and probation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions for the misconduct include public reprimand and supervisory measures; in this matter the Respondent is publicly reprimanded and shall serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During probation the practitioner is permitted to practice before the USPTO unless subsequently suspended or excluded; probation terms can be enforced as described in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure (Order to Show Cause and potential suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that the Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct during probation, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not order immediate suspension for up to six (6) months; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record; and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond. If after consideration the OED Director still believes noncompliance occurred, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure is sequential: issuance of Order to Show Cause, 15-day response period, internal review, and then referral to USPTO Director for suspension; any review sought by Respondent of such suspension does not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension on PTO credentials (customer numbers and PKI certificates)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended, the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates; Respondent shall not use any USPTO Customer Number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated, and may not obtain a USPTO Customer Number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative consequences to access and filing capabilities are explicit and automatic upon suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for disciplinary notices (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and publish a notice that is materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Reprimand and Probation' in the Official Gazette and in the OED Electronic FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a template notice summarizing the misconduct, sanction, and relevant factual background to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in (1) addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as (i) an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary records may be relied upon in subsequent matters and can increase severity of future sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent: mishandling of client or firm funds constitutes serious ethical misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner's mishandling of funds collected from clients on behalf of his or her law firm may constitute ethical misconduct for which they may be appropriately sanctioned; cited authorities include In re Fredericksen, In re Casey, Disciplinary Counsel v. Riek, In re Siderits, and In re Christian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cited cases exemplify outcomes (suspension, disbarment) for misappropriation, failure to maintain records, manipulation of billable hours, conversion, commingling, or poor management of funds; they are used to justify the gravity of sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual bearing of costs under the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural/settlement term allocating litigation and administrative costs between parties.
